newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says natural monopolies prices unjustified.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says natural monopolies prices unjustified.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin told a joint meeting of both houses of parliament on Thursday that natural monopolies' prices were unjustifiably high, fuelling a non-payments crisis.
"I do not want the natural monopolies to be the main source of non-payments in the economy," Yeltsin said.
Yeltsin said natural gas, electricity and rail transport were the most strategic monopolies, and criticised them for raising prices too high, thus creating debts.
"This year we will take their activities under strict control of the state," he added.
In a written document accompanying the speech, Yeltsin ordered the government to set up a plan within three months to regulate prices and control costs at natural monopolies.
He criticised subsidies and privileged rates to end-users for hurting other industrial sectors and attacked a system of cross subsidies through non-budgetary means.
Federal organs set up but not yet functioning should be working by mid-1997 to regulate natural monopolies, the document said.
